frameTime.probe: tests/narcosis.spec.js, 'a frame with every narcosis effect on takes no longer than one without': two pages resume the same dive at 20 m, one at index 0.94 (all four effects on throughout: still above 0.45 at its last frame), one at 0, both holding a fin key and the vent. Frames are stepped by hand; each sample is one frame's real time with gl.finish(), so the GPU's work (SwiftShader in headless Chromium) is included. 30 warm-up frames each, then 30 interleaved rounds of 10 (6 of 50 before c9f8c44), 300 samples each. Since 19b575c each page reports the Performance-evidence metrics of docs/decisions.md as src/diagnostics.js summarize() computes them: sampleCount, minMs, medianMs, p95Ms, p99Ms, maxMs (a percentile is the ceil(q * n)th sample), longFrameCount (frames over 16.67 ms) and totalTimeAboveBudgetMsPer1000 (their excess over 16.67 ms, per 1,000 frames). The assertion stays median-based: narcosed median <= sober median * 1.5 + 1 ms (1.25x + 0.5 ms before c9f8c44). Since 745fd32 (Codex round 1) the probe runs at two pinned configurations, test.use({ viewport, deviceScaleFactor }): 1280x720 at DPR 1, drawing a 1214x654 backing, and 390x844 at DPR 2, the renderer's resolution cap, drawing 780x1688; it asserts window.devicePixelRatio and records the measured backing in each result. Runs before 745fd32 used the spec's default viewport at DPR 1, not 960x540, which is the visual check's size.

frameTime.reading: By configuration, medians narcosed against sober, on the measured build. 1280x720 at DPR 1, alone: 1.2/1.2, 1.6/1.5, 1.5/1.5 ms; in the full suite: 2.3/2.2 ms. 390x844 at DPR 2 (780x1688 backing), alone: 1.3/1.1, 1.4/1.1, 1.5/1.2 ms; in the full suite: 2.2/2.1 ms. At DPR 2 the narcosed page's time above 16.67 ms per 1,000 frames is higher in all three alone runs (94/62, 334/68, 256/116 ms); at DPR 1 it is mixed (70/64, 226/133, 145/205). Earlier runs at the default viewport, all listed above: alone the medians agreed within 0.4 ms; in the full suite the narcosed page was slower in eight of nine runs, by 0.2 to 1.3 ms. The full-screen vignette is a real alpha blend in SwiftShader's CPU rasteriser, and under load it shows. The bound, 1.5x + 1 ms on the median, allows that at both configurations and stays well under a 16.67 ms frame; it is a coarse cost bound, not a claim that the effects cost nothing. Every run has long frames on both pages, so the machine was busy beyond this probe: the port lock keeps other e2e runs out, not other work. SwiftShader in headless Chromium is diagnostic evidence, not physical-device acceptance (docs/decisions.md). The check does not tell a GPU filter apart: a Pixi BlurFilter on the world passes it (V6), unlike legacy's Canvas 2D ctx.filter; the wreck-narcosis reference frame and the parity test fail on a blur (V6).

rule: Owner decision on #220 (2026-10-07): the tunnel vision above index 0.15 is one pre-rendered overlay sprite whose alpha follows the index, with no per-frame gradient; the wobble above 0.25 is an offset of the world container, on the scene's real-time clock; blur and grayscale are not ported, recorded in docs/decisions.md as a deliberate departure. The wobble is off under prefers-reduced-motion (docs/decisions.md, Accessibility: reduced-motion support).
change: src/render/narcosis-view.ts holds legacy's vignette alpha, min(0.7, (index - 0.15) * 0.82), and wobble, sin(t * 0.002) * str across and cos(t * 0.0015) * str * 0.5 down with str = (index - 0.25) * 8 px, t in ms of the scene's elapsedRealS. src/render/pixi-renderer.ts draws legacy's radial gradient (clear at 0.3 of the shorter side, black at 0.7 of the longer) on a canvas once per viewport size, as one sprite over the world and not moved by the wobble; each frame sets its alpha and visibility from PresentationState.narcosisIndex and offsets the world container by the wobble, unless prefers-reduced-motion is set. scripts/pixi-visual-check.mjs adds wreck-narcosis, a dive resumed from its own first save at 20 m, index 0.9, frames pinned. docs/decisions.md records blur and grayscale as a deliberate departure. Pre-review pass 1: the migration catalogue's gameOver.info.nitrogenNarcosis.prevention3 (en, de) names only the cues the migration shows, tunnel vision, keys that do not respond and drifting up or down, not legacy's colour loss nor the wobble alone, which reduced motion turns off; claims register NARCOSIS-001 records the departure. The departure row in docs/decisions.md names the five checkpoints that reach it and cites tests/unit/narcosis-view.test.ts.

counterChecks.method: Each mutation applied by a script to a file backed up beforehand, the client rebuilt, the named checks run under the port lock with --retries=0, then the file restored from its backup and compared with filecmp (shallow=False): byte for byte identical in every case, and the client rebuilt. Re-taken on 19b575c, a local commit not on the remote, whose trees provenanceNote records; it differs from the measured da626c0 only by one German catalogue line and spec comments. V3 and V5 use the typechecking forms (this.#reducedMotion?.matches && false) and wobble.x * 0. V6 adds BlurFilter to the pixi.js import, a module constant new BlurFilter({ strength: 3 }) and this.#world.filters = index > 0.15 ? [it] : [] in render().
